questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid spherical body of radius $R$, density $\rho$, and specific heat capacity $s$ is initially at temperature $T_0$. It is placed in a vacuum chamber at absolute zero and cools by emitting thermal radiation as a perfect blackbody (Stefan-Boltzmann constant $\sigma$). If the rate of fall of temperature depends on its instantaneous temperature $T$ as $T^x$, and the time $t$ taken for its temperature to drop from $T_0$ to $\dfrac{T_0}{2}$ is proportional to $\sigma^\alpha \rho^\beta s^\gamma R^\delta T_0^{-3}$, then which of the following sets of values is correct?
questions.solution:
The rate of heat loss from the spherical body by thermal radiation is given by the Stefan-Boltzmann law:

$\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \sigma A T^4$

where $A = 4 \pi R^2$ is the surface area of the sphere.

The heat loss is also related to the rate of fall of temperature by:

$\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = -m s \dfrac{dT}{dt}$

where $m = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \rho$ is the mass of the sphere.

Equating the two expressions:

$-\left(\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \rho\right) s \dfrac{dT}{dt} = \sigma (4 \pi R^2) T^4$

$-\dfrac{dT}{dt} = \dfrac{3 \sigma}{\rho s R} T^4$

The rate of fall of temperature is proportional to $T^4$, which gives $x = 4$.

To find the time taken for the temperature to drop from $T_0$ to $\dfrac{T_0}{2}$, we integrate the expression:

$\int_{T_0}^{\dfrac{T_0}{2}} T^{-4} dT = -\int_{0}^{t} \dfrac{3 \sigma}{\rho s R} dt$

$\left[ \dfrac{T^{-3}}{-3} \right]_{T_0}^{\dfrac{T_0}{2}} = -\dfrac{3 \sigma}{\rho s R} t$

$-\dfrac{1}{3} \left( \left(\dfrac{T_0}{2}\right)^{-3} - T_0^{-3} \right) = -\dfrac{3 \sigma}{\rho s R} t$

$\dfrac{1}{3} \left( 8 T_0^{-3} - T_0^{-3} \right) = \dfrac{3 \sigma}{\rho s R} t$

$\dfrac{7}{3} T_0^{-3} = \dfrac{3 \sigma}{\rho s R} t$

$t = \dfrac{7 \rho s R}{9 \sigma} T_0^{-3}$

From this, we can see that $t \propto \sigma^{-1} \rho^1 s^1 R^1 T_0^{-3}$.

Comparing this with $t \propto \sigma^\alpha \rho^\beta s^\gamma R^\delta T_0^{-3}$, we get:

$\alpha = -1$

$\beta = 1$

$\gamma = 1$

$\delta = 1$

Thus, the correct set of values is $x=4, \alpha=-1, \beta=1, \gamma=1, \delta=1$.

Answer: $x=4, \alpha=-1, \beta=1, \gamma=1, \delta=1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A straight canal has motorboats departing from two terminals at opposite ends. The motorboats depart at regular intervals of $T$ minutes in both directions and travel at a constant speed $v$. A tourist is riding a bicycle on a path parallel to the canal at a constant speed of $20 \text{ km/h}$. The tourist observes that a motorboat overtakes him every $18 \text{ minutes}$, and he crosses a motorboat moving in the opposite direction every $6 \text{ minutes}$. Determine the speed of the motorboats ($v$) and the departure interval ($T$).
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the motorboats be $v$ and the departure interval be $T$.

The distance between two consecutive motorboats moving in the same direction is $vT$.

The speed of the tourist is $u = 20 \text{ km/h}$.

When the motorboats overtake the tourist, they are moving in the same direction. The relative speed is $v - u$. The time interval between consecutive overtakes is $18 \text{ minutes}$.

$(v - 20) \times \dfrac{18}{60} = v \times \dfrac{T}{60} \Rightarrow vT = 18(v - 20)$

When the motorboats cross the tourist in the opposite direction, the relative speed is $v + u$. The time interval between consecutive crossings is $6 \text{ minutes}$.

$(v + 20) \times \dfrac{6}{60} = v \times \dfrac{T}{60} \Rightarrow vT = 6(v + 20)$

Equating the two expressions for $vT$:

$18(v - 20) = 6(v + 20)$

$3(v - 20) = v + 20$

$3v - 60 = v + 20$

$2v = 80 \Rightarrow v = 40 \text{ km/h}$

Substituting $v = 40 \text{ km/h}$ into the second equation:

$40T = 6(40 + 20)$

$40T = 360 \Rightarrow T = 9 \text{ min}$

Answer: $40 \text{ km/h}, 9 \text{ min}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A wooden crate is released from rest at the top of a ramp inclined at $37^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. When the ramp is perfectly smooth, the crate reaches the bottom with a speed $v$. When the ramp is rough, the crate reaches the bottom with a speed of $\dfrac{v}{3}$. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the rough ramp?

(Take $\tan 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{4}$)
questions.solution:
Let the length of the ramp be $L$ and the angle of inclination be $\theta = 37^{\circ}$.

For the smooth ramp, the acceleration of the crate is $a_1 = g \sin \theta$.
Using the equation of motion, $v^2 = 2a_1L = 2gL \sin \theta$.

For the rough ramp, the acceleration of the crate is $a_2 = g \sin \theta - \mu_k g \cos \theta$.
The velocity at the bottom is $\dfrac{v}{3}$, so $\left(\dfrac{v}{3}\right)^2 = 2a_2L = 2gL(\sin \theta - \mu_k \cos \theta)$.

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get:
$\dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{\sin \theta - \mu_k \cos \theta}{\sin \theta}$

$\dfrac{1}{9} = 1 - \mu_k \cot \theta$

$\mu_k \cot \theta = 1 - \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{8}{9}$

$\mu_k = \dfrac{8}{9} \tan \theta$

Given $\tan 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, substituting this value:
$\mu_k = \dfrac{8}{9} \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform horizontal beam of mass $6\text{ kg}$ and length $L$ is hinged to a vertical wall at one end. The other end is supported by a light inextensible wire attached to the same wall, making an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the beam. A block of mass $9\text{ kg}$ is suspended from the free end of the beam. The horizontal component of the reaction force exerted by the hinge on the beam is (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Let the length of the beam be $L$.

Taking torque about the hinge to be zero for rotational equilibrium:

$T \sin 30^{\circ} \times L = 60 \times \dfrac{L}{2} + 90 \times L$

$T \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 30 + 90$

$T = 240\text{ N}$

For horizontal equilibrium, the net force in the horizontal direction is zero. The horizontal component of the hinge reaction $R_x$ balances the horizontal component of the tension:

$R_x = T \cos 30^{\circ}$

$R_x = 240 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 120\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$

Answer: $120\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bullet $P$ of mass $30\text{ g}$ moving with a speed of $200\text{ m/s}$ penetrates a target and comes to rest after travelling a distance of $10\text{ cm}$ inside it. Another bullet $Q$ of mass $20\text{ g}$ moving with a speed of $300\text{ m/s}$ penetrates another target and comes to rest after travelling $20\text{ cm}$ inside it. If $F_P$ and $F_Q$ are the average resistive forces offered by the targets to bullets $P$ and $Q$ respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{F_P}{F_Q}$ is :
questions.solution:
Using the work-energy theorem, the work done by the resistive force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the bullet.

$F \times s = \dfrac{1}{2} m u^2 \Rightarrow F = \dfrac{m u^2}{2 s}$

For bullet $P$:

$F_P = \dfrac{30 \times 10^{-3} \times (200)^2}{2 \times 0.10} = \dfrac{30 \times 10^{-3} \times 40000}{0.2} = 6000 \text{ N}$

For bullet $Q$:

$F_Q = \dfrac{20 \times 10^{-3} \times (300)^2}{2 \times 0.20} = \dfrac{20 \times 10^{-3} \times 90000}{0.4} = 4500 \text{ N}$

The ratio of the average resistive forces is:

$\dfrac{F_P}{F_Q} = \dfrac{6000}{4500} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small block of mass $m$ is placed at the highest point of a smooth fixed sphere of radius $R$. It is given a horizontal initial speed $v_1$ such that it slides down the surface. The block loses contact with the sphere at a point where the radius vector makes an angle $\alpha$ with the upward vertical. The ratio of the block's speed $v_2$ at the point of losing contact to its initial speed $v_1$ is :
questions.solution:
At the point where the block loses contact with the sphere, the normal reaction $N$ becomes zero.
The equation of motion along the radial direction is given by:
$mg \cos \alpha - N = \dfrac{m v_2^2}{R}$

Setting $N = 0$, we get:
$mg \cos \alpha = \dfrac{m v_2^2}{R} \Rightarrow v_2^2 = gR \cos \alpha$

Applying the principle of conservation of mechanical energy between the highest point and the point of losing contact:
$\dfrac{1}{2} m v_1^2 + mgR = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_2^2 + mgR \cos \alpha$

Multiplying by $\dfrac{2}{m}$ throughout:
$v_1^2 + 2gR = v_2^2 + 2gR \cos \alpha$
$v_1^2 = v_2^2 - 2gR(1 - \cos \alpha)$

From the radial equation, we have $gR = \dfrac{v_2^2}{\cos \alpha}$. Substituting this into the energy equation:
$v_1^2 = v_2^2 - 2 \left( \dfrac{v_2^2}{\cos \alpha} \right) (1 - \cos \alpha)$

$v_1^2 = v_2^2 \left[ 1 - \dfrac{2(1 - \cos \alpha)}{\cos \alpha} \right]$

$v_1^2 = v_2^2 \left[ \dfrac{\cos \alpha - 2 + 2 \cos \alpha}{\cos \alpha} \right]$

$v_1^2 = v_2^2 \left( \dfrac{3 \cos \alpha - 2}{\cos \alpha} \right)$

Rearranging to find the ratio $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}$:
$\dfrac{v_2^2}{v_1^2} = \dfrac{\cos \alpha}{3 \cos \alpha - 2}$

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \left( \dfrac{\cos \alpha}{3 \cos \alpha - 2} \right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Answer: $\left( \dfrac{\cos \alpha}{3 \cos \alpha - 2} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ is projected with an initial speed of $14 \text{ m/s}$ on a rough horizontal surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface is $0.2$. After traveling a distance of $24 \text{ m}$, the block collides head-on with a massive stationary bumper. It rebounds and travels a distance of $9 \text{ m}$ before coming to rest. What is the magnitude of the impulse imparted by the bumper to the block? (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
The deceleration of the block due to kinetic friction is given by:

$a = -\mu_k g = -0.2 \times 10 = -2 \text{ m/s}^2$

Let $v_1$ be the velocity of the block just before it collides with the bumper. Using the third equation of motion:

$v_1^2 = u^2 + 2a d_1$

$v_1^2 = (14)^2 + 2(-2)(24)$

$v_1^2 = 196 - 96 = 100 \Rightarrow v_1 = 10 \text{ m/s}$

Let $v_2$ be the velocity of the block just after rebounding. Since it comes to rest after traveling $d_2 = 9 \text{ m}$:

$0 = v_2^2 + 2a d_2$

$v_2^2 = 2(2)(9) = 36 \Rightarrow v_2 = 6 \text{ m/s}$

The impulse $J$ imparted by the bumper is equal to the change in momentum of the block. Taking the initial direction of motion as positive:

$J = m(v_f - v_i) = m(-v_2 - v_1)$

$J = 2(-6 - 10) = -32 \text{ N s}$

The magnitude of the impulse is $32 \text{ N s}$.

Answer: $32 \text{ N s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform horizontal circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating freely about a vertical axis passing through its center at an angular speed of $40\text{ rpm}$. Two small blocks, each of mass $\dfrac{M}{4}$, are initially fixed at diametrically opposite points on the edge of the disc. If the blocks are slowly moved to a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the center along the diameter, what will be the new angular speed of the system?
questions.solution:
The initial moment of inertia of the system is the sum of the moment of inertia of the disc and the two blocks at the edge.

$I_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + 2\left(\dfrac{M}{4}R^2\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 = MR^2$

When the blocks are moved to a distance of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ from the center, the new moment of inertia is:

$I_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + 2\left(\dfrac{M}{4}\left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + \dfrac{1}{8}MR^2 = \dfrac{5}{8}MR^2$

Since no external torque acts on the system, angular momentum is conserved:

$I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$

Substituting the given values:

$MR^2 \times 40 = \dfrac{5}{8}MR^2 \times \omega_2$

$\omega_2 = 40 \times \dfrac{8}{5} = 64\text{ rpm}$

Answer: $64\text{ rpm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A space probe is studying a newly discovered spherical planet of radius $R$. The probe measures the gravitational acceleration at a height of $\dfrac{R}{2}$ above the planet's surface to be $a_1$. Later, the probe moves to a higher orbit at a height of $2R$ above the surface, where the gravitational acceleration is measured to be $a_2$. What is the ratio $\dfrac{a_1}{a_2}$?
questions.solution:
The gravitational acceleration at a distance $r$ from the center of a planet is given by $g = \dfrac{GM}{r^2}$.

For the first orbit, the height is $h_1 = \dfrac{R}{2}$, so the distance from the center is $r_1 = R + \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{3R}{2}$.

The acceleration is $a_1 = \dfrac{GM}{\left(\dfrac{3R}{2}\right)^2} = \dfrac{4GM}{9R^2}$.

For the second orbit, the height is $h_2 = 2R$, so the distance from the center is $r_2 = R + 2R = 3R$.

The acceleration is $a_2 = \dfrac{GM}{(3R)^2} = \dfrac{GM}{9R^2}$.

The ratio of the accelerations is $\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4GM}{9R^2}}{\dfrac{GM}{9R^2}} = 4$.

Thus, the ratio is $4 : 1$.

Answer: $4 : 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider a narrow capillary tube dipped vertically into a large container of liquid with density $\rho$ and surface tension $S$. The liquid rises in the tube to a height $h$ above the flat surface of the liquid in the container, forming a spherical meniscus. What is the radius of curvature $R$ of this meniscus?
questions.solution:
The pressure difference across a spherical meniscus of radius of curvature $R$ is given by $\Delta P = \dfrac{2S}{R}$.

This pressure difference is balanced by the hydrostatic pressure of the liquid column of height $h$, which is $\Delta P = \rho g h$.

Equating the two expressions for the pressure difference:

$\dfrac{2S}{R} = \rho g h$

Solving for $R$:

$R = \dfrac{2S}{\rho g h}$

Answer: $R = \dfrac{2S}{\rho g h}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three composite rectangular slabs A, B, and C of equal thickness and equal cross-sectional area are joined end-to-end in series. Their thermal conductivities are $3K$, $2K$, and $K$ respectively. The free end of slab A is maintained at $66^\circ\text{C}$ and the free end of slab C is maintained at $0^\circ\text{C}$. Assuming steady-state heat conduction and no heat loss from the lateral surfaces, what is the temperature difference across the middle slab B?
questions.solution:
The thermal resistance of a slab is given by $R = \dfrac{L}{kA}$.

For the three slabs A, B, and C having equal thickness $L$ and equal cross-sectional area $A$, the thermal resistances are:
$R_A = \dfrac{L}{3KA}$
$R_B = \dfrac{L}{2KA}$
$R_C = \dfrac{L}{KA}$

Since the slabs are connected in series, the rate of heat flow $H$ is the same through all of them. The temperature difference across any slab is proportional to its thermal resistance ($\Delta T = HR$).

The ratio of temperature differences across the slabs is:
$\Delta T_A : \Delta T_B : \Delta T_C = R_A : R_B : R_C = \dfrac{1}{3} : \dfrac{1}{2} : 1 = 2 : 3 : 6$

The total temperature difference across the composite slab is:
$\Delta T_{total} = 66^\circ\text{C} - 0^\circ\text{C} = 66^\circ\text{C}$

The temperature difference across the middle slab B is:
$\Delta T_B = \dfrac{3}{2 + 3 + 6} \times \Delta T_{total} = \dfrac{3}{11} \times 66^\circ\text{C} = 18^\circ\text{C}$

Answer: $18^\circ\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two rigid, thermally insulated tanks A and B are connected by a narrow tube fitted with a closed valve. Tank A has a volume of $5$ L and contains an ideal gas at a pressure of $300$ kPa and a temperature of $400$ K. Tank B has a volume of $15$ L and contains the same ideal gas at a pressure of $100$ kPa and a temperature of $300$ K. When the valve is opened and the gases are allowed to mix, what will be the final equilibrium pressure of the system?
questions.solution:
Conservation of internal energy for the insulated system gives:

$U_A + U_B = U_f$

$n_A C_v T_A + n_B C_v T_B = (n_A + n_B) C_v T_f$

$n_A T_A + n_B T_B = n_f T_f$

From the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$, which gives $nT = \dfrac{PV}{R}$. Substituting this into the energy equation:

$\dfrac{P_A V_A}{R} + \dfrac{P_B V_B}{R} = \dfrac{P_f V_f}{R}$

$P_A V_A + P_B V_B = P_f (V_A + V_B)$

Substituting the given values:

$300(5) + 100(15) = P_f (5 + 15)$

$1500 + 1500 = 20 P_f$

$3000 = 20 P_f$

$P_f = 150$ kPa

Answer: $150$ kPa

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal gas is enclosed in a cylinder fitted with a frictionless, movable piston of area $0.04 \text{ m}^2$. The gas is heated by an electrical coil of resistance $50 \ \Omega$ carrying a current of $2 \text{ A}$ for $10 \text{ s}$. During this process, the gas expands at a constant pressure of $10^5 \text{ Pa}$ and its internal energy increases by $1200 \text{ J}$. The distance moved by the piston is:
questions.solution:
Heat supplied by the electrical coil is given by Joule's law of heating:

$Q = I^2 R t$

$Q = (2)^2 \times 50 \times 10 = 2000 \text{ J}$

According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$Q = \Delta U + W$

$2000 = 1200 + W$

$W = 800 \text{ J}$

Work done by the gas at constant pressure is:

$W = P \Delta V = P A d$

Substituting the given values:

$800 = 10^5 \times 0.04 \times d$

$800 = 4000 \times d$

$d = \dfrac{800}{4000} = 0.2 \text{ m}$

$d = 20 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $20 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A rigid storage tank of volume $0.0831 \mathrm{~m}^{3}$ contains $1.4 \mathrm{~kg}$ of Nitrogen gas ($N_{2}$) at a temperature of $300 \mathrm{~K}$. A valve is accidentally left open, and some gas escapes. When the valve is closed, the gauge pressure of the tank is found to be $5 \mathrm{~atm}$. Assuming the temperature of the gas remains constant, the mass of Nitrogen that escaped from the tank is :
[Given: $R = 8.31 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}$, molecular mass of $N_{2} = 28 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, $1 \mathrm{~atm} = 10^{5} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$]
questions.solution:
The final absolute pressure of the gas in the tank is the sum of the gauge pressure and the atmospheric pressure.

$P = P_{gauge} + P_{atm} = 5 \mathrm{~atm} + 1 \mathrm{~atm} = 6 \mathrm{~atm} = 6 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$

Using the ideal gas equation, the final number of moles of Nitrogen in the tank is:

$n_{f} = \dfrac{PV}{RT}$

Substituting the given values:

$n_{f} = \dfrac{6 \times 10^{5} \times 0.0831}{8.31 \times 300} = 20 \mathrm{~mol}$

The final mass of Nitrogen remaining in the tank is:

$m_{f} = n_{f} \times M = 20 \mathrm{~mol} \times 28 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} = 560 \mathrm{~g} = 0.56 \mathrm{~kg}$

The mass of Nitrogen that escaped from the tank is the difference between the initial and final mass:

$\Delta m = m_{i} - m_{f} = 1.4 \mathrm{~kg} - 0.56 \mathrm{~kg} = 0.84 \mathrm{~kg}$

Answer: $0.84 \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $4\text{ kg}$ is executing simple harmonic motion on a smooth horizontal surface with an amplitude $A$ and frequency $\nu$, under the restoring force of an ideal spring. When the block passes through its mean position, a lump of putty of mass $5\text{ kg}$ is dropped vertically onto the block and sticks to it. What will be the new frequency ($\nu'$) and new amplitude ($A'$) of the oscillation?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two blocks, $X$ and $Y$, are executing simple harmonic motion on smooth horizontal surfaces. Block $X$ has mass $M$ and is attached to a spring of force constant $K$. Block $Y$ has mass $2M$ and is attached to a spring of force constant $8K$. If both blocks cross their respective mean positions with identical speeds, what is the ratio of the amplitude of block $X$ to the amplitude of block $Y$?
questions.solution:
For block $X$, the angular frequency is $\omega_X = \sqrt{\dfrac{K}{M}}$.

For block $Y$, the angular frequency is $\omega_Y = \sqrt{\dfrac{8K}{2M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4K}{M}} = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{K}{M}}$.

The maximum speed of a block executing simple harmonic motion is given by $v = A\omega$, which occurs at the mean position.

Given that both blocks have identical speeds at their mean positions, $v_X = v_Y$.

$A_X \omega_X = A_Y \omega_Y$

$A_X \sqrt{\dfrac{K}{M}} = A_Y \left(2\sqrt{\dfrac{K}{M}}\right)$

$\dfrac{A_X}{A_Y} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

The ratio of the amplitude of block $X$ to the amplitude of block $Y$ is $2 : 1$.

Answer: $2 : 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical small conducting spheres $P$ and $Q$ carry charges of $+8\mu\text{C}$ and $-2\mu\text{C}$ respectively. When placed at a certain distance $r$ apart in vacuum, the magnitude of the attractive electrostatic force between them is $F$. A third identical conducting sphere $R$ carrying an initial charge of $+4\mu\text{C}$ is brought into contact with sphere $P$ first, then with sphere $Q$, and finally removed. If the distance between $P$ and $Q$ remains unchanged, what is the magnitude of the new electrostatic force between them?
questions.solution:
Initial charges on the spheres are $q_P = +8\mu\text{C}$ and $q_Q = -2\mu\text{C}$.

The initial electrostatic force between $P$ and $Q$ is:
$F = \dfrac{k |q_P| |q_Q|}{r^2} = \dfrac{k (8)(2)}{r^2} = \dfrac{16k}{r^2}$

When the identical sphere $R$ with charge $q_R = +4\mu\text{C}$ is brought into contact with $P$, they share the total charge equally:
$q_P' = q_R' = \dfrac{q_P + q_R}{2} = \dfrac{8 + 4}{2} = +6\mu\text{C}$

Next, sphere $R$ (now carrying $+6\mu\text{C}$) is brought into contact with $Q$ (carrying $-2\mu\text{C}$). They share the total charge equally:
$q_Q' = q_R'' = \dfrac{q_R' + q_Q}{2} = \dfrac{6 + (-2)}{2} = +2\mu\text{C}$

The new charges on $P$ and $Q$ are $q_P' = +6\mu\text{C}$ and $q_Q' = +2\mu\text{C}$.

The new electrostatic force between $P$ and $Q$ at the same distance $r$ is:
$F' = \dfrac{k |q_P'| |q_Q'|}{r^2} = \dfrac{k (6)(2)}{r^2} = \dfrac{12k}{r^2}$

Taking the ratio of the new force to the initial force:
$\dfrac{F'}{F} = \dfrac{\dfrac{12k}{r^2}}{\dfrac{16k}{r^2}} = \dfrac{12}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow F' = \dfrac{3F}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3F}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric dipole of moment $6.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ C m}$ is placed in a uniform electric field of magnitude $5.0 \times 10^4 \text{ N/C}$. Initially, the dipole is held at an angle of $120^{\circ}$ with respect to the field direction. The work done by an external agent to slowly rotate the dipole until it becomes anti-parallel to the electric field is:
questions.solution:
The work done by an external agent to slowly rotate an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is equal to the change in its potential energy.

$W = \Delta U = U_f - U_i$

The potential energy of a dipole in an electric field is given by $U = -pE \cos \theta$.

$W = -pE \cos \theta_2 - (-pE \cos \theta_1) = pE (\cos \theta_1 - \cos \theta_2)$

Given $p = 6.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ C m}$, $E = 5.0 \times 10^4 \text{ N/C}$, $\theta_1 = 120^{\circ}$, and $\theta_2 = 180^{\circ}$ (anti-parallel).

$W = (6.0 \times 10^{-8}) \times (5.0 \times 10^4) (\cos 120^{\circ} - \cos 180^{\circ})$

$W = 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \left(-\dfrac{1}{2} - (-1)\right)$

$W = 3.0 \times 10^{-3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ J}$

Answer: $1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has a capacitance $C_0$ when there is air between its plates, which are separated by a distance $d$. Two dielectric slabs are inserted between the plates, parallel to them. The first slab has a thickness of $\dfrac{d}{2}$ and a dielectric constant of $4$. The second slab has a thickness of $\dfrac{d}{4}$ and an unknown dielectric constant $K$. The remaining space between the plates is filled with air. If the new equivalent capacitance of the system becomes $2C_0$, what is the value of $K$?
questions.solution:
Initial capacitance is $C_0 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$.

When dielectric slabs are inserted, the equivalent capacitance is given by $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{t_1}{K_1} + \dfrac{t_2}{K_2} + \dfrac{t_3}{K_3}}$.

The thicknesses of the regions are $t_1 = \dfrac{d}{2}$, $t_2 = \dfrac{d}{4}$, and the remaining air space is $t_3 = d - \left(\dfrac{d}{2} + \dfrac{d}{4}\right) = \dfrac{d}{4}$.

Substituting the given values:

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{d/2}{4} + \dfrac{d/4}{K} + \dfrac{d/4}{1}}$

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d \left(\dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4K} + \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}$

$C = \dfrac{C_0}{\dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4K}}$

Given that $C = 2C_0$, we have:

$2C_0 = \dfrac{C_0}{\dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4K}}$

$\dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{1}{4K} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{4K} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{8} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$4K = 8 \Rightarrow K = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform wire of resistance $R$ is cut into $6$ equal segments. Three of these segments are connected in series to form a combination $X$. The remaining three segments are connected in parallel to form a combination $Y$. If $X$ and $Y$ are then connected in parallel with each other, what is the equivalent resistance of the entire arrangement?
questions.solution:
Resistance of the uniform wire = $R$

When cut into $6$ equal segments, the resistance of each segment is $r = \dfrac{R}{6}$

Combination $X$ consists of $3$ segments in series.

Resistance of $X$, $R_X = 3r = 3 \times \dfrac{R}{6} = \dfrac{R}{2}$

Combination $Y$ consists of $3$ segments in parallel.

Resistance of $Y$, $R_Y = \dfrac{r}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{R}{6} = \dfrac{R}{18}$

Combinations $X$ and $Y$ are connected in parallel.

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R_X} + \dfrac{1}{R_Y}$

$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{2}{R} + \dfrac{18}{R} = \dfrac{20}{R}$

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{20}$

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{20}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four resistors are connected to form a quadrilateral ABCD such that the resistance of arm AB is 10 $\Omega$, arm BC is 20 $\Omega$, arm CD is 60 $\Omega$, and arm AD is 30 $\Omega$. A 50 $\Omega$ resistor is connected between the junctions B and D. A battery of EMF 12 V and internal resistance 1.5 $\Omega$ is connected across the junctions A and C. What is the current drawn from the battery?
questions.solution:
The given circuit is a Wheatstone bridge with the battery connected across junctions A and C.

The resistances of the arms are $R_{AB} = 10 \, \Omega$, $R_{BC} = 20 \, \Omega$, $R_{AD} = 30 \, \Omega$, and $R_{CD} = 60 \, \Omega$.

Checking the balance condition of the Wheatstone bridge:

$\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac{10}{20} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{CD}} = \dfrac{30}{60} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{BC}} = \dfrac{R_{AD}}{R_{CD}}$, the bridge is balanced. Therefore, no current flows through the $50 \, \Omega$ resistor connected between junctions B and D.

The equivalent resistance of the upper branch ABC is $R_{ABC} = 10 + 20 = 30 \, \Omega$.

The equivalent resistance of the lower branch ADC is $R_{ADC} = 30 + 60 = 90 \, \Omega$.

The equivalent resistance of the bridge $R_{eq}$ is the parallel combination of $R_{ABC}$ and $R_{ADC}$:

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{30 \times 90}{30 + 90} = \dfrac{2700}{120} = 22.5 \, \Omega$

The total resistance of the circuit, including the internal resistance of the battery $r = 1.5 \, \Omega$, is:

$R_{total} = R_{eq} + r = 22.5 + 1.5 = 24 \, \Omega$

The current drawn from the battery is:

$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{total}} = \dfrac{12}{24} = 0.5 \, A$

Answer: $0.5 A$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the given circuit, a $20\text{ V}$ ideal battery is connected across the terminals P and S. An ideal ammeter is connected between nodes Q and R. Determine the reading of the ammeter.
questions.solution:
An ideal ammeter has zero resistance, so it acts as a short circuit between nodes Q and R. This means nodes Q and R are at the same potential.

The circuit can be simplified as two parallel combinations in series. The $2\ \Omega$ and $4\ \Omega$ resistors are in parallel, and the $6\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$ resistors are in parallel.

The equivalent resistance of the first parallel combination (between P and Q/R) is:
$R_1 = \dfrac{2 \times 4}{2 + 4} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}\ \Omega$

The equivalent resistance of the second parallel combination (between Q/R and S) is:
$R_2 = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = \dfrac{18}{9} = 2\ \Omega$

The total equivalent resistance of the circuit is:
$R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2 = \dfrac{4}{3} + 2 = \dfrac{10}{3}\ \Omega$

The total current drawn from the battery is:
$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{20}{10/3} = 6\text{ A}$

The voltage drop across the first parallel combination is:
$V_1 = I \times R_1 = 6 \times \dfrac{4}{3} = 8\text{ V}$

The current flowing through the $2\ \Omega$ resistor (from P to Q) is:
$I_{PQ} = \dfrac{V_1}{2} = \dfrac{8}{2} = 4\text{ A}$

The voltage drop across the second parallel combination is:
$V_2 = I \times R_2 = 6 \times 2 = 12\text{ V}$

The current flowing through the $6\ \Omega$ resistor (from Q to S) is:
$I_{QS} = \dfrac{V_2}{6} = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2\text{ A}$

Applying Kirchhoff's Current Law at node Q, the current entering the node must equal the current leaving it. Let $I_A$ be the current flowing through the ammeter from Q to R:
$I_{PQ} = I_{QS} + I_A$
$4 = 2 + I_A$
$I_A = 2\text{ A}$

Thus, the reading of the ammeter is $2\text{ A}$.

Answer: $2\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A beam of positively charged particles is moving with a velocity of $4 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~m~s}^{-1}$ along the positive x-axis. It enters a region containing a uniform electric field of $8 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~V~m}^{-1}$ directed along the positive y-axis. To ensure that the particles pass through this region without any deviation, a uniform magnetic field must be applied. What should be the magnitude and direction of this magnetic field?
questions.solution:
For the positively charged particles to pass through the region without any deviation, the net force acting on them must be zero. This means the electric force and the magnetic force must be equal and opposite.

The Lorentz force equation is given by:
$\vec{F} = q\vec{E} + q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) = 0$

$\Rightarrow \vec{E} = -(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$

Given:
Velocity, $\vec{v} = 4 \times 10^5 \hat{i} \text{ m s}^{-1}$
Electric field, $\vec{E} = 8 \times 10^4 \hat{j} \text{ V m}^{-1}$

Substituting these values into the equation:
$8 \times 10^4 \hat{j} = -(4 \times 10^5 \hat{i} \times \vec{B})$

For the cross product $\hat{i} \times \vec{B}$ to result in a $-\hat{j}$ direction, $\vec{B}$ must be in the $\hat{k}$ direction (since $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$). Let $\vec{B} = B \hat{k}$.

$8 \times 10^4 \hat{j} = -[4 \times 10^5 \hat{i} \times (B \hat{k})]$

$8 \times 10^4 \hat{j} = -[4 \times 10^5 B (-\hat{j})]$

$8 \times 10^4 \hat{j} = 4 \times 10^5 B \hat{j}$

Equating the magnitudes:
$B = \dfrac{8 \times 10^4}{4 \times 10^5} = 0.2 \text{ T}$

Thus, the magnetic field must have a magnitude of $0.2 \text{ T}$ and be directed along the positive z-axis ($\hat{k}$).

Answer: $0.2 \mathrm{~T}$ along the positive z-axis

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two square loops, $P$ and $Q$, carry currents in the ratio $3 : 2$. If the side lengths of the loops are in the ratio $1 : 3$, what is the ratio of the magnetic dipole moment of loop $P$ to that of loop $Q$?
questions.solution:
The magnetic dipole moment of a current-carrying loop is given by $M = I A$, where $I$ is the current and $A$ is the area of the loop.

For a square loop of side length $a$, the area is $A = a^2$.

The ratio of the magnetic dipole moments of loops $P$ and $Q$ is

$\dfrac{M_P}{M_Q} = \dfrac{I_P A_P}{I_Q A_Q} = \left(\dfrac{I_P}{I_Q}\right) \left(\dfrac{a_P}{a_Q}\right)^2$

Given $\dfrac{I_P}{I_Q} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and $\dfrac{a_P}{a_Q} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, substituting these values gives

$\dfrac{M_P}{M_Q} = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

The ratio of the magnetic dipole moment of loop $P$ to that of loop $Q$ is $1 : 6$.

Answer: $1 : 6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton and an alpha particle, initially at rest, are accelerated through the same potential difference. They then enter a region of uniform magnetic field perpendicular to their velocities, where they move in circular orbits. What is the ratio of the magnetic moment of the alpha particle's orbit to that of the proton's orbit?
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a particle accelerated through a potential difference $V$ is $K = qV$.

The magnetic moment of a charged particle moving in a circular orbit is given by $M = IA$.

The time period of revolution is $T = \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$, so the equivalent current is $I = \dfrac{q}{T} = \dfrac{q^2 B}{2\pi m}$.

The radius of the circular path is $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$, so the area of the orbit is $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}\right)^2 = \dfrac{2\pi m K}{q^2 B^2}$.

Therefore, the magnetic moment is $M = I A = \left(\dfrac{q^2 B}{2\pi m}\right) \left(\dfrac{2\pi m K}{q^2 B^2}\right) = \dfrac{K}{B} = \dfrac{qV}{B}$.

For a proton, the charge is $q$, so its magnetic moment is $M_p = \dfrac{qV}{B}$.

For an alpha particle, the charge is $2q$, so its magnetic moment is $M_{\alpha} = \dfrac{2qV}{B}$.

The ratio of the magnetic moment of the alpha particle to that of the proton is $\dfrac{M_{\alpha}}{M_p} = \dfrac{2qV/B}{qV/B} = 2$.

Thus, the ratio is $2 : 1$.

Answer: $2 : 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The figure shows a branch of an electrical circuit. At a given instant, the current $I$ flowing from Q to P is $3 \text{ A}$ and it is decreasing at a rate of $4 \text{ A/s}$. If point Q is connected to the ground, what is the electric potential at point P?
questions.solution:
Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) from point Q to point P, we can write the equation for the potential difference:

$V_Q - I R - L \dfrac{dI}{dt} + E = V_P$

Given the parameters in the problem:
$\bullet$ Point Q is grounded, so $V_Q = 0 \text{ V}$.
$\bullet$ The current $I$ flowing from Q to P is $3 \text{ A}$.
$\bullet$ The current is decreasing at a rate of $4 \text{ A/s}$, so the rate of change of current is $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = -4 \text{ A/s}$.
$\bullet$ The resistance $R = 4 \ \Omega$.
$\bullet$ The inductance $L = 0.5 \text{ H}$.
$\bullet$ The battery has an EMF $E = 6 \text{ V}$. Traversing from Q to P, we move from the negative (shorter, thicker line) to the positive (longer, thinner line) terminal, which means there is a potential gain of $+6 \text{ V}$.

Substituting these values into the KVL equation:

$0 - (3 \text{ A})(4 \ \Omega) - (0.5 \text{ H})(-4 \text{ A/s}) + 6 \text{ V} = V_P$

$0 - 12 \text{ V} + 2 \text{ V} + 6 \text{ V} = V_P$

$V_P = -4 \text{ V}$

The electric potential at point P is $-4 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $-4 \text{ V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating voltage of $240 \text{ V}$ (rms) is applied across a series combination of a $12 \,\Omega$ resistor, an inductor of reactance $30 \,\Omega$, and a capacitor of reactance $14 \,\Omega$. What is the rms current drawn from the source and the power factor of the circuit, respectively?
questions.solution:
The net reactance of the series RLC circuit is given by:

$X = X_L - X_C = 30 - 14 = 16 \,\Omega$

The impedance of the circuit is:

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + 16^2} = \sqrt{144 + 256} = 20 \,\Omega$

The rms current drawn from the source is:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} = \dfrac{240}{20} = 12 \text{ A}$

The power factor of the circuit is:

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{12}{20} = 0.6$

Answer: $12 \text{ A}$ and $0.6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A researcher is adjusting a compound microscope to view a bacterial sample. The microscope has an objective lens of focal length $1.5\text{ cm}$ and an eyepiece of focal length $5.0\text{ cm}$. If the researcher wants to achieve a total magnifying power of $200$ for a relaxed eye (normal adjustment), what must be the tube length of the microscope?

(Take the least distance of distinct vision as $25\text{ cm}$)
questions.solution:
The magnifying power of a compound microscope in normal adjustment (relaxed eye) is given by:

$M = \dfrac{L}{f_o} \times \dfrac{D}{f_e}$

where $L$ is the tube length, $f_o$ is the focal length of the objective, $f_e$ is the focal length of the eyepiece, and $D$ is the least distance of distinct vision.

Substituting the given values:

$200 = \dfrac{L}{1.5} \times \dfrac{25}{5.0}$

$200 = \dfrac{L}{1.5} \times 5$

$L = \dfrac{200 \times 1.5}{5}$

$L = 40 \times 1.5 = 60\text{ cm}$

Answer: $60\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An optical system is constructed by placing three thin lenses coaxially in contact. The focal lengths of the three lenses are $f$, $\dfrac{f}{2}$, and $-f$, respectively. If the lateral magnifications produced by these individual lenses are $m_1$, $m_2$, and $m_3$, what is the equivalent power and the total lateral magnification of the system?
questions.solution:
The equivalent power of a combination of thin lenses in contact is the sum of their individual powers.

$P = P_1 + P_2 + P_3$

$P = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2} + \dfrac{1}{f_3}$

Substituting the given focal lengths $f_1 = f$, $f_2 = \dfrac{f}{2}$, and $f_3 = -f$:

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{2}{f} - \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{2}{f}$

For a system of lenses in contact, the total lateral magnification is the product of the lateral magnifications produced by the individual lenses.

$M = m_1 \times m_2 \times m_3 = m_1 m_2 m_3$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{f}$ and $m_1 m_2 m_3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A beam of unpolarised light with intensity $I_0$ falls on a system of three polaroids $P_1$, $P_2$, and $P_3$ arranged in series. The transmission axes of $P_1$ and $P_3$ are perpendicular to each other. If the transmission axis of $P_2$ is inclined at an angle of $15^{\circ}$ with respect to the transmission axis of $P_1$, what will be the intensity of the light transmitted through $P_3$?
questions.solution:
Intensity of light after passing through $P_1$ is $I_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$

Angle between transmission axes of $P_1$ and $P_2$ is $\theta_1 = 15^{\circ}$

Intensity of light after passing through $P_2$ is $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2(15^{\circ}) = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \cos^2(15^{\circ})$

Angle between transmission axes of $P_1$ and $P_3$ is $90^{\circ}$

Angle between transmission axes of $P_2$ and $P_3$ is $\theta_2 = 90^{\circ} - 15^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}$

Intensity of light after passing through $P_3$ is $I_3 = I_2 \cos^2(75^{\circ}) = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \cos^2(15^{\circ}) \cos^2(75^{\circ})$

Since $\cos(75^{\circ}) = \sin(15^{\circ})$, we get:

$I_3 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} (\sin(15^{\circ}) \cos(15^{\circ}))^2$

$I_3 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \left( \dfrac{\sin(30^{\circ})}{2} \right)^2$

$I_3 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \left( \dfrac{1/2}{2} \right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{4} \right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{32}$

Answer: $\dfrac{I_0}{32}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hypothetical atom consists of a particle of mass $m$ moving in a circular orbit around a central stationary nucleus. The potential energy of the particle in this field is given by $U(r) = \alpha r^4$, where $\alpha$ is a positive constant and $r$ is the distance from the center. If Bohr's quantization postulate is applied to this system, how do the radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit ($r_n$) and the kinetic energy of the particle in that orbit ($K_n$) depend on the principal quantum number $n$?
questions.solution:
The potential energy of the particle is given by $U(r) = \alpha r^4$.

The conservative force acting on the particle is $F = -\dfrac{dU}{dr} = -4\alpha r^3$.

The magnitude of this force provides the necessary centripetal force for circular motion:

$\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = 4\alpha r^3$

$mv^2 = 4\alpha r^4$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{4\alpha}{m}} r^2$

According to Bohr's quantization postulate, the angular momentum is quantized:

$mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

Substituting the expression for $v$ into the quantization condition:

$m \left( \sqrt{\dfrac{4\alpha}{m}} r^2 \right) r = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

$\sqrt{4\alpha m} r^3 = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

$r^3 = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi \sqrt{4\alpha m}}$

From this, we can see that the radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit depends on $n$ as:

$r_n \propto n^{1/3}$

The kinetic energy of the particle is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$. Using $mv^2 = 4\alpha r^4$, we get:

$K_n = \dfrac{1}{2}(4\alpha r_n^4) = 2\alpha r_n^4$

Substituting $r_n \propto n^{1/3}$ into the kinetic energy expression:

$K_n \propto (n^{1/3})^4$

$K_n \propto n^{4/3}$

Answer: $r_n \propto n^{1/3}$ ; $K_n \propto n^{4/3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An unpolarized beam of light travelling in a transparent dense medium of refractive index $\sqrt{3}$ is incident on its interface with air at Brewster's angle. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the reflected and refracted light?
options: The reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is $60^{\circ}$.
The transmitted light is completely polarized and the angle of refraction is $60^{\circ}$.
The reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of refraction is $60^{\circ}$.
Both reflected and transmitted light are partially polarized with an angle of $90^{\circ}$ between them.
questions.solution:
For light travelling from a dense medium of refractive index $n_1$ to a rarer medium of refractive index $n_2$, Brewster's angle $\theta_B$ is given by:

$\tan \theta_B = \dfrac{n_2}{n_1}$

Given $n_1 = \sqrt{3}$ and $n_2 = 1$ (air), we have:

$\tan \theta_B = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta_B = 30^{\circ}$

At Brewster's angle, the reflected light is completely polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

The angle of incidence is $i = \theta_B = 30^{\circ}$. By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection is also $30^{\circ}$.

To find the angle of refraction $r$, we use Snell's law:

$n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r$

$\sqrt{3} \sin 30^{\circ} = 1 \times \sin r$

$\sqrt{3} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \sin r \Rightarrow \sin r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow r = 60^{\circ}$

Alternatively, at Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular, so $i + r = 90^{\circ}$.

$30^{\circ} + r = 90^{\circ} \Rightarrow r = 60^{\circ}$

Thus, the reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of refraction is $60^{\circ}$.

Answer: The reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of refraction is $60^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of an electron revolving in the third orbit of a singly ionized helium atom ($He^+$) to that of an electron revolving in the second orbit of a doubly ionized lithium atom ($Li^{2+}$)?
questions.solution:
According to Bohr's quantization rule, the angular momentum is $mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.

The de Broglie wavelength of an electron is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$.

Substituting $mv$ from the first equation, we get $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi r}{n}$.

The radius of the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen-like atom is $r \propto \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.

Therefore, the de Broglie wavelength is proportional to $\lambda \propto \dfrac{n}{Z}$.

For the electron in the third orbit of $He^+$, $n_1 = 3$ and $Z_1 = 2$.

$\lambda_1 \propto \dfrac{3}{2}$

For the electron in the second orbit of $Li^{2+}$, $n_2 = 2$ and $Z_2 = 3$.

$\lambda_2 \propto \dfrac{2}{3}$

The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths is $\dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2}}{\dfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{9}{4}$.

Answer: $9 : 4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two ideal diodes $D_1$ and $D_2$ are connected in two parallel branches between nodes A and B as shown in the figure. An alternating voltage source $V(t) = 200 \sin(50\pi t)$ volts is applied across the nodes, where $V(t)$ represents the potential difference $V_A - V_B$. At time $t = 10 \text{ ms}$, which of the following statements is correct regarding the biasing of the diodes?
options: $D_1$ is reverse biased, $D_2$ is forward biased
$D_1$ is forward biased, $D_2$ is reverse biased
questions.solution:
The potential difference between nodes A and B is given by $V(t) = V_A - V_B = 200 \sin(50\pi t)$.

At time $t = 10 \text{ ms} = 10 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s} = 0.01 \text{ s}$, the voltage is:

$V(0.01) = 200 \sin(50\pi \times 0.01)$

$V(0.01) = 200 \sin(0.5\pi) = 200 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 200 \text{ V}$

Since $V(0.01) \gt 0$, we have $V_A - V_B \gt 0$, which implies $V_A \gt V_B$. Thus, node A is at a higher potential than node B.

From the circuit diagram, the anode (p-side) of diode $D_1$ is connected to node A and its cathode (n-side) is connected towards node B. Since $V_A \gt V_B$, $D_1$ is forward biased.

The cathode (n-side) of diode $D_2$ is connected to node A and its anode (p-side) is connected towards node B. Since $V_A \gt V_B$, $D_2$ is reverse biased.

Therefore, $D_1$ is forward biased and $D_2$ is reverse biased.

Answer: $D_1$ is forward biased, $D_2$ is reverse biased

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A student uses a Vernier callipers to measure the length of a metal cylinder. The main scale is graduated in millimeters ($1 \text{ M.S.D.} = 1 \text{ mm}$), and $20$ Vernier scale divisions (V.S.D.) coincide with $19$ main scale divisions.

When the jaws of the callipers are brought into contact with each other, the zero of the Vernier scale lies to the left of the main scale zero, and the $8^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale mark.

While measuring the cylinder, the main scale reading is $3.4 \text{ cm}$ and the $14^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale mark. The true length of the cylinder is:
questions.solution:
$1$ M.S.D. = $1$ mm = $0.1$ cm

$20$ V.S.D. = $19$ M.S.D.

$1$ V.S.D. = $\dfrac{19}{20}$ M.S.D. = $0.95$ mm

Least count (L.C.) = $1$ M.S.D. - $1$ V.S.D. = $1$ mm - $0.95$ mm = $0.05$ mm = $0.005$ cm

Since the zero of the Vernier scale lies to the left of the main scale zero, the zero error is negative.

Zero error = $- (N - n) \times \text{L.C.}$

Zero error = $- (20 - 8) \times 0.005$ cm = $-12 \times 0.005$ cm = $-0.06$ cm

Measured value = M.S.R. + $n' \times \text{L.C.}$

Measured value = $3.4$ cm + $14 \times 0.005$ cm = $3.4$ cm + $0.07$ cm = $3.47$ cm

True length = Measured value - Zero error

True length = $3.47$ cm - ($-0.06$ cm) = $3.53$ cm

Answer: $3.53 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A neutron of mass $m$ and a photon have the same de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$. What is the ratio of the energy of the photon to the kinetic energy of the neutron? (Here $c$ is the speed of light and $h$ is Planck's constant)
questions.solution:
The energy of the photon is given by $E_p = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

The momentum of the neutron is $p = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$

The kinetic energy of the neutron is $E_n = \dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}$

The ratio of the energy of the photon to the kinetic energy of the neutron is:

$\dfrac{E_p}{E_n} = \dfrac{\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}}{\dfrac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}} = \dfrac{2mc\lambda}{h}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2mc\lambda}{h}$

questions.solution:
The circuit consists of three logic gates:

1. A NAND gate with inputs $A$ and $B$. Its output is $Y_1 = \overline{A \cdot B}$.

2. An AND gate with inputs $Y_1$ and $B$. Its output is $Y_2 = Y_1 \cdot B = (\overline{A \cdot B}) \cdot B$.

3. A NOR gate with both inputs connected to $Y_2$. This acts as a NOT gate. Its output is $Y = \overline{Y_2 + Y_2} = \overline{Y_2}$.

Now, simplify the Boolean expression for $Y$:

$Y_2 = (\overline{A \cdot B}) \cdot B$

Using De Morgan's law, $\overline{A \cdot B} = \bar{A} + \bar{B}$.

$Y_2 = (\bar{A} + \bar{B}) \cdot B = \bar{A} \cdot B + \bar{B} \cdot B$

Since $\bar{B} \cdot B = 0$, we have $Y_2 = \bar{A} \cdot B$.

The final output is $Y = \overline{Y_2} = \overline{\bar{A} \cdot B}$.

Using De Morgan's law again:

$Y = \overline{\bar{A}} + \bar{B} = A + \bar{B}$

Constructing the truth table for $Y = A + \bar{B}$:

For $A = 0, B = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 0 + \bar{0} = 0 + 1 = 1$

For $A = 0, B = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 0 + \bar{1} = 0 + 0 = 0$

For $A = 1, B = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 1 + \bar{0} = 1 + 1 = 1$

For $A = 1, B = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 1 + \bar{1} = 1 + 0 = 1$

This matches the truth table given in option (A).

Answer:
ABY
001
010
101
111

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory provides the direct theoretical basis for the law of conservation of mass?
options: Atoms of different elements combine in fixed, simple whole number ratios to form compounds.
Atoms can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
All atoms of a given element have identical properties, including identical mass.
questions.solution:
The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

According to Dalton's atomic theory, atoms are indivisible particles, which cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. This postulate provides the direct theoretical basis for the law of conservation of mass, as the total number of atoms of each element remains constant before and after the reaction, ensuring the total mass remains unchanged.

Answer: Atoms can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following five samples of substances:
A. 88 g of $\mathrm{CO}_2$
B. 96 g of $\mathrm{O}_2$
C. 34 g of $\mathrm{NH}_3$
D. 36 g of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
E. 40 g of $\mathrm{Ne}$

Which of the given samples contain an identical total number of atoms?
(Given atomic masses in $\mathrm{u}$: $\mathrm{H}=1$, $\mathrm{C}=12$, $\mathrm{N}=14$, $\mathrm{O}=16$, $\mathrm{Ne}=20$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\mathrm{CO}_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44 \text{ g/mol}$
Moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2 = \dfrac{88}{44} = 2 \text{ moles}$
Total atoms in A $= 2 \times 3 \times N_A = 6 N_A$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{O}_2 = 2 \times 16 = 32 \text{ g/mol}$
Moles of $\mathrm{O}_2 = \dfrac{96}{32} = 3 \text{ moles}$
Total atoms in B $= 3 \times 2 \times N_A = 6 N_A$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}_3 = 14 + 3 \times 1 = 17 \text{ g/mol}$
Moles of $\mathrm{NH}_3 = \dfrac{34}{17} = 2 \text{ moles}$
Total atoms in C $= 2 \times 4 \times N_A = 8 N_A$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} = 2 \times 1 + 16 = 18 \text{ g/mol}$
Moles of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} = \dfrac{36}{18} = 2 \text{ moles}$
Total atoms in D $= 2 \times 3 \times N_A = 6 N_A$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{Ne} = 20 \text{ g/mol}$
Moles of $\mathrm{Ne} = \dfrac{40}{20} = 2 \text{ moles}$
Total atoms in E $= 2 \times 1 \times N_A = 2 N_A$

Samples A, B, and D contain an identical total number of atoms ($6 N_A$).

Answer: A, B and D only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the shortest wavelength of the Lyman series for a hydrogen atom is $x$, then the longest wavelength of the Paschen series for a $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion is:
questions.solution:
The Rydberg formula for the wavelength of emitted radiation is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R Z^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$

For the shortest wavelength of the Lyman series for a hydrogen atom, $Z = 1$, $n_1 = 1$, and $n_2 = \infty$. Substituting these values:

$\dfrac{1}{x} = R (1)^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty} \right) = R$

For the longest wavelength of the Paschen series for a $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion, $Z = 2$, $n_1 = 3$, and $n_2 = 4$. Let this wavelength be $\lambda$. Substituting these values:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R (2)^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{3^2} - \dfrac{1}{4^2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = 4R \left( \dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{16} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = 4R \left( \dfrac{16 - 9}{144} \right) = 4R \left( \dfrac{7}{144} \right) = \dfrac{7R}{36}$

Substituting $R = \dfrac{1}{x}$ into the equation:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{7}{36x}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{36x}{7}$

Answer: $\dfrac{36x}{7}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What are the energy of the second Bohr orbit of $\mathrm{Be}^{3+}$ and the radius of the third Bohr orbit of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ respectively?
[Given: $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} = 2.18 \times 10^{-18} \text{ J}, \mathrm{a}_0 = 52.9 \text{ pm}$]
questions.solution:
The energy of the $n$-th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by $E_n = -R_H \times \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$

For $\mathrm{Be}^{3+}$, the atomic number $Z = 4$. For the second orbit, $n = 2$.

$E_2 = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{4^2}{2^2} = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times 4 = -8.72 \times 10^{-18} \text{ J}$

The radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit is given by $r_n = a_0 \times \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$

For $\mathrm{He}^{+}$, the atomic number $Z = 2$. For the third orbit, $n = 3$.

$r_3 = 52.9 \times \dfrac{3^2}{2} = 52.9 \times 4.5 = 238.05 \text{ pm}$

Answer: $-8.72 \times 10^{-18} \text{ J}$ and $238.05 \text{ pm}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following electronic configurations of neutral atoms:
A. $[\mathrm{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^4$
B. $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$
C. $[\mathrm{Kr}] 4d^{10} 5s^2$
D. $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^2 6p^2$
E. $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$

Which of the above configurations represent d-block elements?
questions.solution:
The block of an element is determined by the subshell in which the last electron enters.

A. $[\mathrm{Ne}] 3s^2 3p^4$: The last electron enters the $3p$ subshell, so it is a p-block element (Group 16).

B. $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$: The last electron enters the $3d$ subshell, so it is a d-block element (Group 8).

C. $[\mathrm{Kr}] 4d^{10} 5s^2$: The last electron enters the $4d$ subshell, so it is a d-block element (Group 12).

D. $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^2 6p^2$: The last electron enters the $6p$ subshell, so it is a p-block element (Group 14).

E. $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$: The last electron enters the $3d$ subshell, so it is a d-block element (Group 6).

Therefore, configurations B, C, and E represent d-block elements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following sequences of molecules and their associated properties:

(I) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2 \gt \mathrm{CHCl}_3$ : Dipole moment
(II) $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{Te} \gt \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S} \gt \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ : Bond angle
(III) $\mathrm{CO} \gt \mathrm{CO}_2 \gt \mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$ : $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length
(IV) $\mathrm{NO}^+ \gt \mathrm{NO} \gt \mathrm{NO}^-$ : Bond order

Which of the above sequences are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I): The dipole moment of chloromethanes decreases as the number of chlorine atoms increases due to the vector addition of individual bond moments. The experimental values are $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl}$ ($1.87$ D) $\gt\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ ($1.60$ D) $\gt\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ ($1.04$ D). This sequence is correct.

Statement (II): The bond angle of group 16 hydrides decreases down the group. As the electronegativity of the central atom decreases, the bond pairs move further away from the central atom, decreasing the bond pair-bond pair repulsion. The correct order is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ ($104.5^\circ$) $\gt\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}$ ($92.1^\circ$) $\gt\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{Te}$ ($90^\circ$). This sequence is incorrect.

Statement (III): The bond order of $\mathrm{CO}$ is $3$, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is $2$, and $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$ is $1.33$. Since bond length is inversely proportional to bond order, the correct order of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length is $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-} \gt \mathrm{CO}_2 \gt \mathrm{CO}$. This sequence is incorrect.

Statement (IV): The total number of electrons in $\mathrm{NO}^+$, $\mathrm{NO}$, and $\mathrm{NO}^-$ are $14$, $15$, and $16$ respectively. According to molecular orbital theory, their bond orders are $3$, $2.5$, and $2$ respectively. The correct order of bond order is $\mathrm{NO}^+ \gt \mathrm{NO} \gt \mathrm{NO}^-$. This sequence is correct.

Therefore, only sequences I and IV are correct.

Answer: I and IV only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The potential energy profile for a hypothetical reaction $X \rightarrow Y$ is shown in the given figure. Based on the graph, what is the enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) for this reaction?
questions.solution:
From the given potential energy profile:

Enthalpy of reactant $X$, $H_X = 40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
Enthalpy of product $Y$, $H_Y = 90\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

The enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) for the reaction is given by the difference in potential energy between the products and the reactants:

$\Delta H = H_{\text{products}} - H_{\text{reactants}}$
$\Delta H = H_Y - H_X$
$\Delta H = 90 - 40 = +50\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $+50\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a reversible gas-phase reaction,
$\mathrm{X(g)} + \mathrm{Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Z(g)}$
the rate constant for the forward reaction is 82 times the rate constant for the backward reaction at 500 K. The value of equilibrium constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ for the reaction at 500 K is:
[Given : $\mathrm{R} = 0.082 \mathrm{~L~atm~mol^{-1}~K^{-1}}$]
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant in terms of concentration, $K_{c}$, is given by the ratio of the forward and backward rate constants:

$K_{c} = \dfrac{k_{f}}{k_{b}}$

Given that $k_{f} = 82 k_{b}$, we have:

$K_{c} = 82$

For the reaction $\mathrm{X(g)} + \mathrm{Y(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Z(g)}$, the change in the number of moles of gas is:

$\Delta n_{g} = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants} = 1 - (1 + 1) = -1$

The relationship between $K_{p}$ and $K_{c}$ is:

$K_{p} = K_{c} (RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$

Substituting the given values ($R = 0.082 \mathrm{~L~atm~mol^{-1}~K^{-1}}$ and $T = 500 \mathrm{~K}$):

$K_{p} = 82 \times (0.082 \times 500)^{-1}$

$K_{p} = \dfrac{82}{41} = 2.0$

Answer: $2.0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following equilibrium for the synthesis of sulfur trioxide:
$2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g}) \quad \Delta H = -198 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Which of the following conditions will favor the maximum yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$?
A. Lower temperature
B. Higher temperature
C. Higher pressure
D. Addition of $\mathrm{O}_2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathrm{g})$ with $\Delta H = -198 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

According to Le Chatelier's principle:

The reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H \lt 0$). Lowering the temperature favors the forward reaction, increasing the yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$. Thus, condition A is correct.

The number of moles of gaseous reactants is $3$ and gaseous products is $2$. Since the forward reaction proceeds with a decrease in the number of moles of gas, increasing the pressure shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction. Thus, condition C is correct.

Adding a reactant ($\mathrm{O}_2$) increases its concentration, which shifts the equilibrium in the forward direction to consume the added reactant. Thus, condition D is correct.

Therefore, conditions A, C, and D favor the maximum yield of $\mathrm{SO}_3$.

Answer: A, C and D only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Hydrogen sulfide ($H_2S$) is a weak diprotic acid that ionizes in two successive steps in an aqueous solution, with ionization constants $K_{a_1}$ and $K_{a_2}$. If $K_{eq}$ represents the overall ionization constant for the complete dissociation of $H_2S$ into $S^{2-}$ ions, which of the following statements are correct?

A. $pK_{eq} = pK_{a_1} + pK_{a_2}$
B. $pK_{a_1} \gt pK_{a_2}$
C. $H_2S$ is a stronger acid than $HS^-$
D. $K_{eq} = \dfrac{K_{a_1}}{K_{a_2}}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The ionization steps of $H_2S$ are:

$H_2S \rightleftharpoons H^+ + HS^-$ with ionization constant $K_{a_1}$

$HS^- \rightleftharpoons H^+ + S^{2-}$ with ionization constant $K_{a_2}$

The overall reaction is:

$H_2S \rightleftharpoons 2H^+ + S^{2-}$ with overall ionization constant $K_{eq}$

From the equations, $K_{eq} = K_{a_1} \times K_{a_2}$.

Taking the negative logarithm on both sides:

$-\log K_{eq} = -\log K_{a_1} - \log K_{a_2}$

$pK_{eq} = pK_{a_1} + pK_{a_2}$

Thus, statement A is correct and statement D is incorrect.

For a polyprotic acid, the first ionization constant is always greater than the second because it is more difficult to remove a positively charged proton from a negatively charged ion ($HS^-$) than from a neutral molecule ($H_2S$).

$K_{a_1} \gt K_{a_2}$

Since $pK_a = -\log K_a$, a larger $K_a$ corresponds to a smaller $pK_a$.

$pK_{a_1} \lt pK_{a_2}$

Thus, statement B is incorrect.

Since $K_{a_1} \gt K_{a_2}$, $H_2S$ is a stronger acid than $HS^-$.

Thus, statement C is correct.

Therefore, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the respective oxidation states of the underlined atoms in $\mathrm{\underline{O}F_2}$, $\mathrm{Li\underline{H}}$, and $\mathrm{K_2\underline{Cr}_2O_7}$?
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{OF_2}$, fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen and has an oxidation state of $-1$. Let the oxidation state of oxygen be $x$.

$x + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +2$

In $\mathrm{LiH}$, lithium is an alkali metal with an oxidation state of $+1$. Let the oxidation state of hydrogen be $y$.

$+1 + y = 0 \Rightarrow y = -1$

In $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$, potassium has an oxidation state of $+1$ and oxygen has an oxidation state of $-2$. Let the oxidation state of chromium be $z$.

$2(+1) + 2z + 7(-2) = 0$

$2 + 2z - 14 = 0$

$2z = 12 \Rightarrow z = +6$

The respective oxidation states are $+2$, $-1$, and $+6$.

Answer: $+2, -1, \text{ and } +6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An analytical chemist needs to perform the following four separations:
(I) Separation of a mixture of ether (b.p. $308\text{ K}$) and toluene (b.p. $384\text{ K}$)
(II) Separation of two miscible liquids having a boiling point difference of $12\text{ K}$
(III) Purification of an organic liquid that decomposes at its normal boiling point
(IV) Separation of $o$-nitrophenol from a mixture containing $p$-nitrophenol

Which of the following sequences correctly identifies the most appropriate distillation techniques for (I), (II), (III), and (IV) respectively?
options: Fractional distillation, Simple distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure, Steam distillation
Simple distillation, Fractional distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure, Steam distillation
Simple distillation, Fractional distillation, Steam distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure
Steam distillation, Fractional distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure, Simple distillation
questions.solution:
For (I), simple distillation is used for separating liquids having a boiling point difference greater than $25\text{ K}$. Here, the difference is $384\text{ K} - 308\text{ K} = 76\text{ K}$.

For (II), fractional distillation is used for separating miscible liquids having a boiling point difference less than $25\text{ K}$. Here, the difference is $12\text{ K}$.

For (III), distillation under reduced pressure is used for purifying liquids that decompose at or near their normal boiling points. Lowering the pressure decreases the boiling point, preventing decomposition.

For (IV), steam distillation is used to separate steam-volatile compounds from non-steam-volatile ones. $o$-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas $p$-nitrophenol is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

The correct sequence is Simple distillation, Fractional distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure, Steam distillation.

Answer: Simple distillation, Fractional distillation, Distillation under reduced pressure, Steam distillation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Observe the given compounds I, II, and III. Identify the correct decreasing order of bond dissociation energy for the $\mathrm{C-H}$ bonds marked with an asterisk (*).
questions.solution:
The bond dissociation energy (BDE) of a $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond is inversely proportional to the stability of the carbon free radical formed after its homolytic cleavage.

Let us analyze the radicals formed from each compound:

Compound I: Homolytic cleavage of the marked $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond generates an allylic radical ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2^\bullet}$). This radical is highly stabilized by resonance.

Compound II: Cleavage of the marked $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond generates an $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridized carbon radical ($\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv C^\bullet}$). The unpaired electron resides in an $\mathrm{sp}$ orbital with 50% s-character, making it highly unstable as the electron is held tightly by the nucleus. Thus, this bond is the strongest.

Compound III: Cleavage of the marked $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond generates a secondary alkyl radical ($\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH^\bullet}$). This radical is stabilized by hyperconjugation (6 $\alpha$-hydrogens) but is less stable than the resonance-stabilized allylic radical.

The order of stability of the resulting free radicals is: I $ \gt $ III $ \gt $ II.

Since a more stable radical corresponds to a lower bond dissociation energy, the decreasing order of BDE is the reverse of the radical stability order.

Therefore, the decreasing order of BDE is II $ \gt $ III $ \gt $ I.

Answer: II $ \gt $ III $ \gt $ I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The given flowchart illustrates various methods for the preparation of benzene. Identify the correct set of reagents A, B, and C required for these conversions.
options: A = Red hot iron tube at 873 K; B = Sodalime, $\Delta$; C = Zn dust, $\Delta$
A = $Mo_2O_3$ at 773 K; B = Sodalime, $\Delta$; C = Na metal, $\Delta$
A = Red hot iron tube at 873 K; B = Aqueous NaOH, $\Delta$; C = Zn dust, $\Delta$
A = $Cr_2O_3$ at 773 K; B = $NaHCO_3$, $\Delta$; C = warm $H_2O$
questions.solution:
The given flowchart shows three different methods for the preparation of benzene.

Reaction A represents the cyclic polymerization of ethyne. When ethyne is passed through a red hot iron tube at $873\text{ K}$, it undergoes cyclic polymerization to form benzene. Thus, A is a red hot iron tube at $873\text{ K}$.

Reaction B represents the decarboxylation of sodium benzoate. When sodium benzoate is heated with sodalime (a mixture of $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{CaO}$), it undergoes decarboxylation to yield benzene. Thus, B is sodalime, $\Delta$.

Reaction C represents the reduction of phenol. Phenol is reduced to benzene when its vapours are passed over heated zinc dust. Thus, C is Zn dust, $\Delta$.

Comparing these with the given options, the correct set of reagents is A = Red hot iron tube at $873\text{ K}$; B = Sodalime, $\Delta$; C = Zn dust, $\Delta$.

Answer: A = Red hot iron tube at 873 K; B = Sodalime, $\Delta$; C = Zn dust, $\Delta$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The skeletal structure of a cyclic hydrocarbon is shown in the figure above.

Which of the following is the correct observation when this compound is shaken with aqueous bromine ($Br_2/H_2O$) at room temperature in the absence of light?
options: The reddish-brown colour of the solution is rapidly decolorized due to an addition reaction.
A white precipitate of a polybrominated derivative is immediately formed.
The reddish-brown colour of the bromine water remains unchanged.
The solution turns colourless with brisk effervescence of hydrogen bromide gas.
questions.solution:
The skeletal structure shown in the figure represents cyclohexane, which is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon (cycloalkane).

Aqueous bromine ($Br_2/H_2O$), also known as bromine water, is a reddish-brown solution commonly used to test for unsaturation (presence of carbon-carbon double or triple bonds). Unsaturated compounds undergo rapid electrophilic addition reactions with bromine, causing the reddish-brown colour to decolorize.

Since cyclohexane is a saturated compound containing only single bonds, it does not undergo addition reactions. Furthermore, in the absence of light (UV radiation) or heat, free radical substitution reactions with alkanes do not occur.

Therefore, there will be no reaction between cyclohexane and aqueous bromine under the given conditions, and the reddish-brown colour of the bromine water will remain unchanged.

Answer: The reddish-brown colour of the bromine water remains unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Based on the physical states of the solute and the solvent, identify the incorrect match from the following examples of solutions:
options: Gas in solid : Solution of hydrogen in palladium
Solid in gas : Camphor in nitrogen gas
Liquid in gas : Chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas
Liquid in solid : Copper dissolved in gold
questions.solution:
Solution of hydrogen in palladium is an example of a gas in solid solution, where hydrogen is the gas and palladium is the solid.

Camphor in nitrogen gas is an example of a solid in gas solution, where camphor is the solid and nitrogen is the gas.

Chloroform mixed with nitrogen gas is an example of a liquid in gas solution, where chloroform is the liquid and nitrogen is the gas.

Copper dissolved in gold is an example of a solid in solid solution, as both copper and gold are solids at room temperature. An example of a liquid in solid solution is an amalgam of mercury with sodium.

Thus, the match 'Liquid in solid : Copper dissolved in gold' is incorrect.

Answer: Liquid in solid : Copper dissolved in gold

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assuming complete dissociation of the electrolytes, which of the following aqueous solutions will freeze at the lowest temperature?
questions.solution:
The depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_f = i \times K_f \times m$.

Assuming molarity is approximately equal to molality for dilute aqueous solutions, $\Delta T_f \propto i \times C$, where $i$ is the van 't Hoff factor and $C$ is the concentration.

For $0.4\text{ M}$ Ethylene glycol: It is a non-electrolyte, so $i = 1$.
$i \times C = 1 \times 0.4 = 0.4$

For $0.15\text{ M CaCl}_2$: It dissociates into $3$ ions ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $2\text{Cl}^-$), so $i = 3$.
$i \times C = 3 \times 0.15 = 0.45$

For $0.1\text{ M K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$: It dissociates into $5$ ions ($4\text{K}^+$ and $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$), so $i = 5$.
$i \times C = 5 \times 0.1 = 0.5$

For $0.2\text{ M NaBr}$: It dissociates into $2$ ions ($\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Br}^-$), so $i = 2$.
$i \times C = 2 \times 0.2 = 0.4$

The solution with the highest value of $i \times C$ will have the maximum depression in freezing point and thus the lowest freezing temperature. This corresponds to $0.1\text{ M K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$.

Answer: $0.1\text{ M K}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A binary solution is prepared by mixing 2 moles of liquid P and 3 moles of liquid Q. At a certain temperature, the vapour pressures of pure P and pure Q are 120 mm Hg and 160 mm Hg, respectively. If the experimentally observed total vapour pressure of the mixture is 155 mm Hg, which of the following statements is correct regarding this solution?
options: The process of mixing liquids P and Q is exothermic ($\Delta H_{\text{mix}} \lt  0$).
The solution is capable of forming a maximum boiling azeotrope.
The intermolecular attractive forces between P and Q are weaker than those in pure P and pure Q.
The volume of the resulting solution is less than the sum of the volumes of the unmixed liquids.
questions.solution:
Mole fraction of P, $x_P = \dfrac{2}{2+3} = 0.4$

Mole fraction of Q, $x_Q = \dfrac{3}{2+3} = 0.6$

According to Raoult's law, the ideal vapour pressure of the solution is:

$P_{\text{ideal}} = P_P^\circ x_P + P_Q^\circ x_Q$

$P_{\text{ideal}} = 120 \times 0.4 + 160 \times 0.6 = 48 + 96 = 144 \text{ mm Hg}$

The observed vapour pressure is $155 \text{ mm Hg}$, which is greater than the ideal vapour pressure ($155 \gt 144$). This indicates that the solution shows a positive deviation from Raoult's law.

For a solution showing positive deviation:

1. The intermolecular attractive forces between the different molecules (P-Q) are weaker than those between the similar molecules (P-P and Q-Q).

2. $\Delta H_{\text{mix}} \gt 0$ (endothermic process).

3. $\Delta V_{\text{mix}} \gt 0$ (volume increases on mixing).

4. The solution can form a minimum boiling azeotrope.

Thus, the statement about weaker intermolecular attractive forces between P and Q is correct.

Answer: The intermolecular attractive forces between P and Q are weaker than those in pure P and pure Q.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The molar conductivity of a $0.02 \text{ M}$ solution of propanoic acid is $31.2 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$. What is the percentage dissociation of the acid in this solution?

[Given: Limiting molar conductivities of $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COO}^-$ are $349.6 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $40.4 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively]
questions.solution:
The limiting molar conductivity of propanoic acid is given by Kohlrausch's law:

$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}(\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{5}\text{COOH}) = \lambda^{\circ}(\text{H}^{+}) + \lambda^{\circ}(\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{5}\text{COO}^{-})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda_{m}^{\circ} = 349.6 + 40.4 = 390.0 \text{ S cm}^{2} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

The degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is the ratio of molar conductivity at a given concentration to the limiting molar conductivity:

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_{m}}{\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{31.2}{390.0} = 0.08$

The percentage dissociation is:

$\alpha \times 100 = 0.08 \times 100 = 8.0\%$

Answer: $8.0\%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A chemical reaction has a rate constant of $6.93 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. How much time will it take for the reaction to be $93.75\%$ complete?
(Given : $\log 2 = 0.301$)
questions.solution:
The unit of the rate constant is $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, indicating a first-order reaction.

The half-life of the reaction is given by:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k} = \dfrac{0.693}{6.93 \times 10^{-3}} = 100 \mathrm{~s}$

For $93.75\%$ completion, the percentage of reactant remaining is:

$100\% - 93.75\% = 6.25\%$

The fraction of reactant remaining is:

$\dfrac{6.25}{100} = \dfrac{1}{16} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^4$

This indicates that $4$ half-lives have passed.

Total time required $= 4 \times t_{1/2} = 4 \times 100 \mathrm{~s} = 400 \mathrm{~s}$

Answer: $400 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the set of coordination complexes in which all the species are diamagnetic in nature.
questions.solution:
In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state with a $3d^6$ configuration. Since $\mathrm{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, electrons pair up to give $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. It has zero unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state with a $3d^6$ configuration. $\mathrm{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$, leading to $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. It has zero unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{PtCl}_4\right]^{2-}$, $\mathrm{Pt}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state with a $5d^8$ configuration. For $4d$ and $5d$ series metals, the crystal field splitting is large, resulting in a square planar geometry ($dsp^2$ hybridization) where all electrons are paired. It is diamagnetic.

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^5$). With the strong field ligand $\mathrm{CN}^-$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$, having one unpaired electron (paramagnetic).

In $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_6\right]^{3-}$, $\mathrm{Co}$ is in $+3$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). With the weak field ligand $\mathrm{F}^-$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, having four unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

In $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Fe}$ is in $+2$ oxidation state ($3d^6$). With the weak field ligand $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, having four unpaired electrons (paramagnetic).

Thus, only the first set contains all diamagnetic species.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}, \left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}, \left[\mathrm{PtCl}_4\right]^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following coordination complexes in the increasing order of the wavelength of light absorbed by them:

A. $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$
B. $\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$
C. $\left[\mathrm{Cr}\left(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\right)_6\right]^{3+}$
D. $\left[\mathrm{CrCl}_6\right]^{3-}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The wavelength of light absorbed by a coordination complex is inversely proportional to the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) of the complex, since $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \Delta_o$.

The magnitude of $\Delta_o$ depends on the field strength of the ligands. According to the spectrochemical series, the increasing order of ligand field strength is:
$\mathrm{Cl}^- \lt \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{NH}_3 \lt \mathrm{CN}^-$

Therefore, the order of crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_o$) for the given complexes is:
$\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-} \gt \left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6\right]^{3+} \gt \left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6\right]^{3+} \gt \left[\mathrm{CrCl}_6\right]^{3-}$
$\mathrm{B} \gt \mathrm{A} \gt \mathrm{C} \gt \mathrm{D}$

Since the wavelength of absorbed light is inversely proportional to $\Delta_o$, the increasing order of wavelength of light absorbed is:
$\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{D}$

Answer: $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{A} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to Werner's coordination theory, which of the following empirical formulations of platinum(IV) chloride with ammonia will exhibit the lowest molar conductance in aqueous solution and fail to give a white precipitate with excess $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$?
questions.solution:
tarrow [\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)_6}]Cl_4$ (yields 5 ions, 4 precipitable $Cl^-$ ions)

$\mathrm{PtCl_4 \cdot 5NH_3} \Rightarrow [\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)_5Cl}]Cl_3$ (yields 4 ions, 3 precipitable $Cl^-$ ions)

$\mathrm{PtCl_4 \cdot 4NH_3} \Rightarrow [\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)_4Cl_2}]Cl_2$ (yields 3 ions, 2 precipitable $Cl^-$ ions)

$\mathrm{PtCl_4 \cdot 2NH_3} \Rightarrow [\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_4}]$ (yields 0 ions, 0 precipitable $Cl^-$ ions)

Since $[\mathrm{Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_4}]$ is a neutral complex, it does not ionize in aqueous solution. Therefore, it exhibits the lowest molar conductance (almost zero) and fails to give a white precipitate of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ upon the addition of excess $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{PtCl_4 \cdot 2NH_3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Predict the major product 'Z' in the following sequence of reactions.
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 2-phenylpropene, $C_6H_5-C(CH_3)=CH_2$.

Reaction with $HBr$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide proceeds via a free radical mechanism, resulting in anti-Markovnikov addition. The bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon to form a stable benzylic radical intermediate, which then abstracts a hydrogen atom from $HBr$.

$C_6H_5-C(CH_3)=CH_2 \xrightarrow{\text{HBr, peroxide}} C_6H_5-CH(CH_3)-CH_2Br$

The product 1-bromo-2-phenylpropane undergoes a nucleophilic substitution reaction with $KCN$ in ethanol. The cyanide ion displaces the bromide ion.
